system:
You are the planning lead of a biomedical data-analysis agent. You receive one scientific question, the data provider's description of a dataset, a measured profile of the data, and a list of measured difficulties. Your job is to compile the question into a precise analysis objective that a team could execute and that an auditor could check.

Rules
- The question decides everything: what is estimated, which inputs are allowed, which are forbidden, and what must be compared with what. Do not optimise for the highest score; optimise for answering this question validly.
- Forbidden inputs must each come with the reason they would invalidate an answer to THIS question.
- Acceptance criteria must be checkable. For each one give: a short statement, the key of one deterministic check from the list provided, and the rule by which any threshold is derived from data. Never write a numeric threshold of your own; only a 5% false discovery rate and a 95% confidence level are fixed conventions.
- State the scope of the conclusion: to which units it applies and what it does not show.
- Use only facts given to you. Do not invent dataset properties.
- Be compact so the answer arrives quickly: at most 8 acceptance criteria, at most 6 forbidden inputs, at most 4 conclusion options, and no string longer than 35 words.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else, with exactly these fields:
{
 "question": string (verbatim),
 "task_family": one of the family keys provided,
 "analysis_unit": string,
 "estimand": string (the quantity to be estimated, in one sentence),
 "target": string (what is predicted or compared),
 "allowed_inputs": [string],
 "forbidden_inputs": [string],
 "forbidden_reasons": {forbidden input: reason},
 "required_comparators": [string] (baselines / rulers every plan must be compared with),
 "primary_metric": string,
 "secondary_metrics": [string],
 "acceptance_criteria": [{"id": "A1", "statement": string, "check": check key, "rule": string}],
 "conclusion_options": [string] (the mutually exclusive answers the analysis may end with),
 "conclusion_scope": string,
 "notes": string
}
prompt:
SCIENTIFIC QUESTION:
Given only the RNA profile of a cell, can the ATAC profile measured in that same cell be found again among the ATAC profiles of many candidate cells?

DATASET DESCRIPTION (from the data provider):
name: 10x Genomics Multiome, PBMC from one healthy donor (granulocytes removed, about 10k cells)
unit: cell
description: 'Each development cell has two count vectors measured in the same nucleus: RNA (UMI counts per gene)
  and ATAC (fragment counts per accessibility peak). Held-out cells of the same donor provide ATAC only. A peak
  annotation links each peak to nearby genes with the distance to the transcription start site and a promoter/distal
  flag. Gene start coordinates are available.'
label_provenance:
  statement: The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities
    jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement.
  implication: The annotation may describe the data but must not be used as a model input for held-out cells (it
    cannot be known without their RNA) and must not serve as evaluation truth.
scope_of_inference: cells of the same donor that were not used for training; nothing about other donors
how_predictions_are_scored: 'The evaluator holds the RNA of the held-out cells. Each held-out cell''s RNA reads
  were split at random into two independent halves, A and B (binomial thinning). Every method is scored against
  half B after log-normalisation: for each gene, the Pearson correlation r between predicted and observed values
  across held-out cells. Genes in scope and the cluster number of the cell-type baseline were frozen from development
  cells only and are part of the view.'
rulers:
  ceiling: an RNA-to-RNA model that sees half A of the held-out cells and predicts half B; it marks what measurement
    noise allows
  floor_1_cell_type: cluster cells on ATAC, predict each cell by its cluster's mean expression (cluster number frozen
    from development cells)
  floor_2_gene_activity: sum of ATAC counts over the promoter and nearby peaks of the gene, no learning
  floor_3_depth: prediction from ATAC sequencing depth alone
  floor_4_simple_learners: ridge, k-nearest-neighbour and partial-least-squares regression on the ATAC latent space
decision_rule: '"Reliably predicted" means predicted beyond cell identity. Each in-scope gene is placed in one of
  three groups: (0) cannot be judged - the ceiling itself is not above the permutation null for this gene; (1) not
  beyond the cell-type baseline - the method''s r is not significantly above the cluster-mean baseline''s r; (2)
  predicts variation beyond cell type - the method''s r is significantly above the cluster-mean baseline''s r (paired
  bootstrap over cells, Benjamini-Hochberg across all in-scope genes, false discovery rate 5%). Thresholds come
  from the data by these rules; only the 5% false discovery rate and the 95% confidence level are conventions. An
  answer of "few or no genes are predicted beyond cell type" is acceptable if that is what the evidence shows.'
deliverable: A prediction matrix (held-out cells x in-scope genes, log-normalised scale), the list of genes the
  method claims to predict beyond cell type, and its own estimate of each gene's correlation with an interval.

MEASURED DATA PROFILE:
{
 "n_development_units": 7288,
 "n_held_out_units": 3124,
 "modalities": {
  "rna": {
   "features": 13536,
   "available_for": "development cells only",
   "fraction_zero": 0.8534380530643333,
   "median_counts_per_cell": 3830.0
  },
  "atac": {
   "features": 108377,
   "available_for": "all cells",
   "fraction_zero": 0.9281561742430454,
   "median_counts_per_cell": 20586.5
  }
 },
 "pairing": "both modalities measured in the same cell for every development cell",
 "genes_in_scope": 11282,
 "peak_gene_links": 87029,
 "cell_type_baseline_k": 20
}

MEASURED DIFFICULTIES (most severe first):
- D1 [measurement_noise, severity high] RNA counts are 85.3% zeros (median 3800 UMIs per cell). Splitting each cell's reads into two independent halves, a gene's value in one half correlates with the other half at a median r of 0.111 across 11282 in-scope genes (90th percentile 0.306). Implication: Per-gene correlation with a single noisy reading is bounded well below 1; scores must be read against a noise ceiling, and validating against smoothed or full-depth targets overstates accuracy.
- D2 [class_imbalance, severity high] The provided annotation has 19 cell types in the development set, from 1936 cells (CD14 Mono) down to 15 (Plasma). Implication: Rare populations contribute little to a pooled correlation and are easy to underfit; within-cluster correlation should be reported alongside the pooled one.
- D3 [multiple_comparisons, severity high] 11282 genes are in scope and each gets its own test. Implication: Gene-level claims need false-discovery-rate control across all in-scope genes.
- D4 [label_provenance, severity high] The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement. Implication: The annotation may describe the data but must not be used as a model input for held-out cells (it cannot be known without their RNA) and must not serve as evaluation truth.
- D5 [technical_confounding, severity medium] ATAC depth and RNA depth are correlated across cells (r = 0.36 on the log scale). A model that sees only ATAC depth reaches a mean per-gene r of 0.032. Implication: Report a depth-only baseline; a predictor must beat it before its signal is called biological.
- D6 [strong_baseline, severity medium] Predicting each cell by the mean expression of its ATAC cluster (k = 20, chosen by cross-validation inside the development set) gives a mean per-gene r of 0.130; ridge regression on the ATAC latent space gives 0.143; the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling is 0.194. Implication: Most predictable variation is cell identity. A plan answers the question only through what it predicts beyond the cluster-mean baseline, gene by gene, on the same cells.
- D7 [statistical_power, severity low] With thousands of cells a correlation as small as 0.037 already exceeds 95% of the permutation null (3124 held-out cells will be scored). Implication: Significance against zero is nearly automatic and cannot be the headline; effect size and the comparison with the cell-type baseline carry the conclusion.

TASK FAMILIES (choose one key):
- cross_modal_prediction: Predict one measured modality from another, feature by feature, for units that provide only the source modality.
- incremental_value_classification: Estimate how much a second modality adds to a baseline modality for predicting a class label.
- single_modality_classification: Estimate how well one modality alone predicts a class label.
- cross_modal_retrieval: Match each unit's profile in one modality to its own profile in another modality among many candidates.

DETERMINISTIC CHECKS AVAILABLE TO THE AUDIT (use these keys in acceptance_criteria.check):
- no_forbidden_inputs: the plan uses no input the objective forbids
- correct_split_unit: the plan's own validation keeps each analysis unit (and everything nested in it) on one side of every split
- beats_required_floors: the method's primary metric is above each required floor / comparator on the same units
- beats_simple_reference: the method is compared directly with the simplest valid plan on the same units
- training_converged: training curves exist and the last part of the curve is no longer improving
- scored_on_unsmoothed_truth: scores are computed against measured, unsmoothed values of units not used for fitting
- both_arms_same_units: the comparison arms use the same units and the same missing-value handling
- selection_nested: model or configuration choices were made without the units the reported score is computed on
- interval_reported: the primary estimate comes with a confidence interval at the 95% level
- multiplicity_controlled: claims about many features control the false discovery rate at 5%
- within_budget: the full run fits the declared budget
- deliverable_complete: the required deliverable exists, has the right shape and contains only finite values
text:
{
 "question": "Given only the RNA profile of a cell, can the ATAC profile measured in that same cell be found again among the ATAC profiles of many candidate cells?",
 "task_family": "cross_modal_retrieval",
 "analysis_unit": "Individual cell (single nucleus with co-measured RNA and ATAC in development splits)",
 "estimand": "Out-of-sample Mean Reciprocal Rank of a cell's true paired ATAC profile among unseen candidate ATAC profiles from the same donor, conditioned solely on that cell's measured RNA profile.",
 "target": "Cell-level pairing identity and rank of each unseen query cell's true co-measured ATAC profile within the candidate ATAC pool.",
 "allowed_inputs": [
  "Paired RNA UMI counts and ATAC peak counts from development cells, partitioned by cell into disjoint training and evaluation splits",
  "Ground-truth cell pairing indices on training splits for model fitting and on evaluation splits strictly for scoring retrieval",
  "Peak-to-gene annotations (TSS distances and promoter/distal flags) and gene start coordinates",
  "Unseen ATAC-only held-out cells of the same donor solely as optional additional distractors in the candidate ATAC pool",
  "Development-set WNN cell-type annotations solely for post-hoc stratified reporting by population, never for training, selection, or retrieval"
 ],
 "forbidden_inputs": [
  "Joint WNN cell-type annotations as model inputs or evaluation truth",
  "Query cell ATAC profiles or test-split pairing labels during inference",
  "Other query cells' RNA profiles or test-batch one-to-one assignment constraints",
  "Evaluation RNA or ATAC profiles smoothed or imputed across cells",
  "Evaluation-split cells during feature selection, latent space fitting, or hyperparameter tuning",
  "Candidate cells' held-out or paired RNA profiles during candidate scoring"
 ],
 "forbidden_reasons": {
  "Joint WNN cell-type annotations as model inputs or evaluation truth": "Constructed from joint RNA-ATAC clustering; using them as inputs leaks cross-modal pairing, and matching cell type does not prove same-cell retrieval.",
  "Query cell ATAC profiles or test-split pairing labels during inference": "Directly leaks the ground-truth paired ATAC identity that must be recovered solely from the query cell's RNA profile.",
  "Other query cells' RNA profiles or test-batch one-to-one assignment constraints": "The question conditions on one cell's RNA profile alone; bipartite matching across queries exploits mutual exclusion rather than single-cell retrieval.",
  "Evaluation RNA or ATAC profiles smoothed or imputed across cells": "Cross-cell smoothing leaks graph neighborhood structure across test cells and masks single-cell dropout noise, overstating individual-cell retrieval accuracy.",
  "Evaluation-split cells during feature selection, latent space fitting, or hyperparameter tuning": "Fitting preprocessing, embeddings, or hyperparameters on evaluation cells leaks test-set structure and biases out-of-sample retrieval estimates upward.",
  "Candidate cells' held-out or paired RNA profiles during candidate scoring": "Candidates represent ATAC profiles only; accessing candidate RNA reduces cross-modal retrieval to unimodal RNA-to-RNA matching."
 },
 "required_comparators": [
  "Floor 0 (permutation null): uniform random ranking of unseen candidate ATAC profiles",
  "Floor 1 (sequencing depth): ranking candidate ATAC profiles by log total fragment depth matched to query log RNA UMI depth",
  "Floor 2 (unlearned gene activity): similarity between query log-RNA and candidate ATAC promoter-plus-proximal peak sums from peak-gene links",
  "Floor 3 (coarse cell-type cluster): matching query RNA to candidate ATAC via training-fitted cluster centroids (baseline k=20)",
  "Simple linear reference: ridge, PLS, or CCA alignment between training-fitted RNA and ATAC latent spaces",
  "Noise-ceiling ruler (upper bound): unimodal split-half count self-retrieval via binomial thinning on evaluation cells"
 ],
 "primary_metric": "Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) of the true paired ATAC profile across unseen query cells, using deterministic mid-ranks for ties",
 "secondary_metrics": [
  "Exact top-1 retrieval rate (Recall@1) across unseen query cells",
  "1 - FOSCTTM (mean fraction of non-matching candidate ATAC profiles ranked strictly farther than the true paired profile)",
  "Within-population and macro-averaged MRR and Recall@1 across cell types to evaluate rare populations and sub-cluster resolution",
  "Ratio of cross-modal retrieval MRR to the binomial-thinning unimodal split-half self-retrieval noise ceiling on the same query cells"
 ],
 "acceptance_criteria": [
  {
   "id": "A1",
   "statement": "Retrieval uses only a single query cell's RNA profile and candidate ATAC profiles, without WNN annotations or cross-query bijection constraints.",
   "check": "no_forbidden_inputs",
   "rule": "Zero forbidden inputs used in fitting, tuning, or inference; each query RNA profile is scored independently against the candidate pool."
  },
  {
   "id": "A2",
   "statement": "Each cell and both its RNA and ATAC profiles stay strictly on one side of every train, validation, and test split.",
   "check": "correct_split_unit",
   "rule": "Cell-identifier overlap between training sets and evaluation query or candidate sets must equal zero across all splits."
  },
  {
   "id": "A3",
   "statement": "Feature selection, normalisation scalers, latent representations, and hyperparameters are selected strictly within inner training splits.",
   "check": "selection_nested",
   "rule": "All data-dependent preprocessing and hyperparameter choices are frozen from inner development splits before touching held-out evaluation cells."
  },
  {
   "id": "A4",
   "statement": "Retrieval is scored on measured, unsmoothed single-cell query RNA and unsmoothed candidate ATAC profiles unseen during training.",
   "check": "scored_on_unsmoothed_truth",
   "rule": "Evaluation profiles undergo only per-cell transformations or training-fitted projections, with no cross-cell smoothing or imputation."
  },
  {
   "id": "A5",
   "statement": "All models and comparators are evaluated on identical unseen query cells against the exact same candidate ATAC pool.",
   "check": "both_arms_same_units",
   "rule": "Query cell IDs, candidate pool membership and size, and mid-rank tie handling are identical across every compared arm."
  },
  {
   "id": "A6",
   "statement": "Claims of individual or sub-cluster retrieval require MRR significantly above permutation, sequencing-depth, gene-activity, and coarse cluster floors.",
   "check": "beats_required_floors",
   "rule": "Lower bound of the paired-bootstrap 95% confidence interval for MRR difference (method minus each floor) exceeds zero."
  },
  {
   "id": "A7",
   "statement": "Nonlinear or complex retrieval architectures are benchmarked directly against a simple linear latent alignment on identical evaluation units.",
   "check": "beats_simple_reference",
   "rule": "Complex methods are favoured over the linear reference only when the paired-bootstrap 95% CI for MRR gain excludes zero."
  },
  {
   "id": "A8",
   "statement": "Primary MRR estimates and comparator differences include 95% confidence intervals; population-specific claims control false discovery rate at 5%.",
   "check": "interval_reported",
   "rule": "Paired nonparametric bootstrap over unseen query cells at 95% confidence; Benjamini-Hochberg at 5% FDR across cell populations if stratified claims are made."
  }
 ],
 "conclusion_options": [
  "Yes, at single-cell resolution: retrieval frequently ranks the true paired ATAC profile first and significantly beats coarse cluster, gene-activity, and depth floors, approaching the unimodal split-half noise ceiling.",
  "Partially (sub-cluster neighborhood only): retrieval significantly beats coarse cluster, gene-activity, and depth floors, but single-cell measurement sparsity prevents reliable top-1 recovery of the exact paired ATAC profile.",
  "Cell-type resolution only: retrieval significantly beats random and sequencing-depth floors, but does not significantly exceed coarse cluster-level matching; individual cells within a cell type cannot be distinguished.",
  "No biological retrieval: given only a cell's RNA profile, ranking candidate ATAC profiles does not significantly outperform random permutation or technical sequencing-depth matching on unseen cells."
 ],
 "conclusion_scope": "Applies to unseen granulocyte-depleted PBMCs from this single healthy donor at this sequencing depth and candidate-pool size; establishes nothing about other donors, tissues, granulocytes, or disease states.",
 "notes": "Provider text describes ATAC-to-RNA prediction, whereas this question requires RNA-to-ATAC cell retrieval on nested splits of the 7,288 paired development cells because the 3,124 held-out cells lack RNA."
}
